summary: Rolling model migration triggers intermittent GPU-attach handshake failures, fallbacks and throughput collapse in dedicated cluster
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled rolling migration of a customer-pinned model variant into Acme AI's dedicated pool (prod/us-west), we observed intermittent GPU-attach handshake failures for a subset of new worker attachments. Those failures caused automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model variant for some requests, which in turn led to cascading throughput collapse (p50->p95 regression) for Acme's high-throughput routed endpoints.

Impact:
- Customer Acme AI experienced ~60% drop in request throughput for ~40 minutes during the migration window.
- Elevated latency: p50 increased from 48ms to 220ms, p95 increased from 230ms to 1.8s for affected routes.
- Some requests returned fallback model outputs (smaller quantized variant) unexpectedly.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: acme-dedicated-prod-uswest (GPU types: A100-80GB mixed with A100-40GB)
- Model rollout: acme-domain-tuned-mistral-7b -> mistral-7b-v1 (rolling across 24 workers)
- Time window: 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC -> 2026-03-12 14:50 UTC

Observed behavior / Timeline:
1) 14:10 UTC: Rollout started, controller scheduled replacements of ~2 workers/min.
2) 14:15 UTC: Metric spike in allocator attachment_time_ms and attach_failures.
3) 14:18 UTC: Autoscaler began conservative throttles due to transient attach latencies; some routes hit fallback policy (model_variant: mistral-quant-7b).
4) 14:20-14:45 UTC: Throughput degraded and p95 spiked; multiple attach handshake errors correlated with a subset of hosts showing increased NVMe IO wait.
5) 14:50 UTC: Rollout paused; manual mitigation applied (drain + reattach on different shard).
6) 15:05 UTC: Throughput recovered to baseline after forced evacuations and targeted worker restarts.

Steps to reproduce (non-deterministic):
- In dedicated pool with mixed GPU SKUs, start a rolling replace of 20-30 workers with model variant swap.
- Simultaneously generate sustained short-stream traffic (small batched requests) from a tenant with many small concurrent streams (Acme load generator used 3500 streams @ 5rps each).
- Observe allocator attach latencies, NVMe IO wait, and attach handshake timeouts.

Logs / Evidence:
- Allocator logs: repeated "attach_handshake_timeout" entries from hosts 10.2.41.12, 10.2.41.18 between 14:16-14:28 UTC.
- Metrics: attach_time_ms P90 jumped to 12.3s; attach_fail_rate 4.7%; worker_nvme_io_wait P95 increased 8x on affected hosts.
- Console traces: route-level fallback events showing automatic switch to mistral-quant-7b at 14:19 UTC.
- Slack thread: #support -> thread t12345 (https://slack.redwood.io/archives/C02/support/p16423).
- Related dashboards: Dedicated Pool -> acme-dedicated-prod-uswest (link in related_confluence_pages).

Hypotheses / Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Mixed GPU SKU placement + heavy short-stream fanout caused NVMe IO contention on placement hosts during worker attach, slowing the attach handshake.
- Hypothesis B: The attach handshake backoff is too aggressive on attach latency, causing the router to trigger fallback to quantized variant prematurely.
- Hypothesis C: A noisy tenant (Acme's own high concurrency pattern) amplified attach latency and evicted local caches, increasing NVMe pressure.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Paused the rollout to stop creating new attachments.
- Per-host restarts of the serving sidecar on 5 affected machines.
- Manually increased handshake timeout to 25s for this rollout via feature flag.
- Routed Acme traffic away from two noisy workers to reduce concurrent short-stream fanout.

Recommended next steps / action items:
- SRE to reproduce in staging with mixed GPU SKUs and high small-stream concurrency (assigned: Diego).
- Adjust attach-handshake timeout and backoff policy to better tolerate transient NVMe IO spikes (short-term flag, long-term config).
- Add allocator-level NVMe pressure alerting and per-host attach-rate limiting to avoid cascading failures.
- Eng: evaluate whether worker pre-warming can reduce new attach IO (ticket to follow).

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Rollout paused and partial recovery achieved via restarts and routing mitigations.
- Root cause not yet confirmed; follow-ups scheduled.
